question.problem: Find the derivative of  $f(t)=(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2}\,k$ with respect to $t.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{t}^{2})\,k \\  & =(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t+t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 2t\,k \\  & =t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j+\sqrt{3}t\,k\end{aligned}
$$
